title: $H^0=k$ is equivalent to geometric connectedness
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $X$ be a scheme over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base], with structure morphism $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], which is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and such that $X$ is geometrically reduced over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Let $A=H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be the ring of global sections of the structure sheaf [def-pc-scheme], a $k$-algebra through the ring map $\rho:k\cong\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}k,\mathcal O)\xrightarrow{f^\sharp}\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Then $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, i.e. $\rho$ is bijective, if and only if $X$ is geometrically connected over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] (that is, $X_{k'}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ is connected for every field extension $k'/k$; in particular nonempty).

proof.text: (Finiteness of $A$.) $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian ($k$ is a Noetherian ring) and $f$ is proper, in particular of finite type, so $X$ is Noetherian, in particular locally Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal O_X$ is quasi-coherent and of finite type (generated by the global section $1$), hence coherent [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. By [lem-pc-coherent-hi] (the case $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, $i=0$) $A=H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)$ is a finite $k$-module for the $k$-module structure given by $\rho$, i.e. $\dim_kA<\infty$.

source.place: Lemma 0BUG (lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections), proof of part (1), citing Cohomology of Schemes 02O6 (coherent-lemma-proper-over-affine-cohomology-finite)

proof.text: (Base change of $A$ to a field.) Let $k'/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], $X_{k'}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ [def-pc-base-change] with projections $g':X_{k'}\to X$ and $f':X_{k'}\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$, and $A_{k'}=\Gamma(X_{k'},\mathcal O_{X_{k'}})$, a $k'$-algebra through $f'^\sharp$. The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]: both spectra are one point, the induced map of local rings is $k\to k'$, and $k'$ is a $k$-vector space, hence free and so flat over $k$. Since $f$ is proper, it is quasi-compact and separated, and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine, so the scheme $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine]. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-global-sections-qcqs] (with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $S'=\operatorname{Spec}k'$) the map $A\otimes_kk'\to A_{k'}$, $a\otimes s\mapsto g'^\sharp(a)f'^\sharp(s)$, is a ring isomorphism; it sends $1\otimes s$ to $f'^\sharp(s)$, so it is an isomorphism of $k'$-algebras. In particular, choosing a $k$-basis of $A$, $\dim_{k'}A_{k'}=\dim_kA$.

source.place: Lemma 0BUG, proof of parts (4) and (5): '$A\otimes_k\overline k=H^0(X_{\overline k},\mathcal O_{X_{\overline k}})$ (equality by Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 02KH)'; Lemma 0FD1 (lemma-baby-stein), proof: '$\Gamma(\overline X,\mathcal O_{\overline X})=\overline A$'

proof.text: (Nonemptiness and global sections.) For a scheme $Y$: if $Y$ is empty then $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ is the zero ring (the sheaf axiom for the empty cover of the empty open set); if $y\in Y$ then $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\to\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is a ring map to a local ring, in which $1\neq0$, so $1\neq0$ in $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$. Hence $Y$ is nonempty if and only if $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ is not the zero ring.

source.place: Lemma 0FD1 (lemma-baby-stein), proof, last paragraph: 'So either $X_i$ is empty and $A_i=0$ or ...'

proof.text: ($H^0=k\Rightarrow$ geometrically connected.) Assume $\rho$ is bijective and let $k'/k$ be any field extension. Then $A\otimes_kk'\cong k\otimes_kk'=k'$ as $k'$-algebras, so by step 2 $A_{k'}\cong k'$ is a field. By step 3 $X_{k'}$ is nonempty, and the only idempotents of the field $A_{k'}$ are $0$ and $1$ ($e(1-e)=0$ forces $e=0$ or $e=1$); by [lem-pc-scheme-connected-iff-idempotents] $X_{k'}$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. As $k'$ was arbitrary, $X$ is geometrically connected over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. (This direction does not use that $X$ is geometrically reduced; it is the case $A=k$ of Lemma 0FD1, where $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is one point and its fibre is $X$, argued for every $k'$ at once instead of reducing to $\overline k$.)

source.place: Lemma 0FD2 (lemma-geometrically-reduced-stein), proof: '(1) $\Rightarrow$ (2)' by Lemma 0FD1 (lemma-baby-stein), whose proof shows the fibre over a point of $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ is connected after base change because its global sections are a local ring with only trivial idempotents

proof.text: (Geometrically connected $\Rightarrow H^0=k$.) Assume $X$ geometrically connected. Choose an algebraic closure $k\to\overline k$ [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique]; $\overline k$ is algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. By the definitions [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], $X_{\overline k}$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], in particular nonempty, and reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Put $B=A_{\overline k}=\Gamma(X_{\overline k},\mathcal O_{X_{\overline k}})$. Then: $B$ is a reduced ring, since $X_{\overline k}$ is reduced (the section-wise form of [def-pc-reduced-scheme]); $B$ is finite-dimensional over $\overline k$ with $\dim_{\overline k}B=\dim_kA$ (steps 1 and 2); $B$ is not the zero ring (step 3); and the only idempotents of $B$ are $0$ and $1$ ([lem-pc-scheme-connected-iff-idempotents] applied to the nonempty connected scheme $X_{\overline k}$). By [lem-pc-alg-closed-reduced-algebra-no-idempotents-dim-one] $\dim_{\overline k}B=1$, hence $\dim_kA=1$. Then $A\neq0$, so the ring map $\rho$ from the field $k$ is injective, and as a $k$-linear injection between $1$-dimensional $k$-vector spaces it is bijective: $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$.

source.place: Lemma 0FD2, proof: '(2) $\Rightarrow$ (1)' by Lemma 0BUG part (7); proof of 0BUG parts (4), (5), (7): $A\otimes_k\overline k=H^0(X_{\overline k},\mathcal O_{X_{\overline k}})$ is reduced (as $X$ is geometrically reduced) and has one primitive idempotent (as $X$ is geometrically connected, by part (2)), and then equals $\overline k$, so $A=k$
